intro: The SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam held on 9 October 2026 featured three shifts with varying difficulty levels. Shifts 1 and 2 were reported as Moderate to Easy‑Moderate, while Shift 3 showed a Moderate to Difficult trend, though its full analysis is pending. Candidates’ good attempt rates ranged from 17‑89 questions in Shift 1 to about 85‑90% in Shifts 2 and 3. All figures are unofficial and SSC normalises scores across shifts to ensure comparability.

faqs.q: What was the overall difficulty of the SSC CGL Tier 1 exam on 9 October 2026?
faqs.a: Shifts 1 and 2 were generally rated Moderate to Easy‑Moderate, whereas Shift 3 was reported as Moderate to Difficult. The overall perception varied across sections and shifts.

faqs.q: Which sections were considered easiest on 9 October 2026?
faqs.a: Reasoning and English were frequently described as easy or moderate in Shifts 1 and 2. General Awareness was mostly easy to moderate, while Quantitative Aptitude showed mixed difficulty.

faqs.q: How many questions did candidates attempt successfully on 9 October 2026?
faqs.a: In Shift 1, candidates reported good attempts on 17 to 89 questions. Shifts 2 and 3 showed higher success rates, with about 85‑90% of questions attempted well.

faqs.q: Why is the analysis for Shift 3 on 9 October 2026 incomplete?
faqs.a: Shift 3 is currently marked as "partial" because not all reports have been received. A complete analysis will be added once the remaining data is available.

faqs.q: How does SSC handle score comparison across different shifts for the 9 October 2026 exam?
faqs.a: SSC normalises scores across shifts to account for any variation in difficulty, ensuring that candidates are evaluated on a comparable basis regardless of the shift they attended.
